With respect, it is cold comfort and unfair to the victim to have to spend considerable amounts to be compensated for his or her medical bills and have to wait for a significant period before he or she can obtain such compensation.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, I hope that the Ministry can look into making insurance for personal devices more affordable so that more users can sign up for such insurance.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I take the point which the Senior Minister of State has made about it being too onerous to make it mandatory for users of PMDs or cyclists to purchase insurance.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, having such insurance not only protects the user but the third party who has been injured by the act of the user as such parties may receive compensation from the insurer of the user.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It would reduce the need for victims to go to Court to obtain compensation.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I would advocate that a culture of mediating dispute arising from the use of shared paths will be better than depending on the Courts.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I have a few points of clarifications before I end.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As we all know, when an accident occurs, it might cause the involved party to be in a state of panic and shock such that he or she might not be able to react or properly respond to what has just occurred.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is not clear from the Bill whether such drivers in such state of shock should face prosecution under this clause should he or she not comply with the series of duties provided under this clause.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Further, clause 23(1)(b) provides that the driver must, as far as circumstances permit, immediately render such assistance as he or she can.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I am worried that there might be situations where the driver's assistance puts the injured party in a worse situation or further exacerbates his or her injuries.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: For the safety of those involved in the event of an accident, I hope that the Ministry can reconsider the necessity of this clause.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify what liabilities and responsibilities would such owners owe to involved parties when an accident occurs after such private land have been declared as a public path?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I think this was also reflected by our colleague Dr Teo Ho Pin.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, under clause 27, such proprietor or occupier has a duty to maintain such way-finding signs at their own cost.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I am puzzled as to why the cost of doing so is not borne by the Authority when such signs are for the benefit of the public at large.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Given that it is a criminal offence, clarity on what conduct constitutes obstructions would be necessary so that users are aware of what they are and avoid acting in a manner that would run afoul of the law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I stand in support of the Bill, I have several concerns to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Ministry be monitoring the amount of conflicts on a public path and reviewing the classification?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And if so, how often will such reviews be conducted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that bicycles will be allowed on footpaths, shared paths and the road.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I remain concerned about allowing bicycles on public paths as I have no doubt that accidents will occur and, of course, have already occurred numerous times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At my last Meet-the-People Session, I met a resident who was knocked down from the back by a bicycle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The cyclist did stop and said sorry but immediately rode off, leaving her with a fractured wrist.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am especially concerned about children using the public paths.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They would be more difficult to spot by the cyclists, and accidents will probably result in more serious injuries and they would be more difficult to avoid as their movements are more erratic as they are often playing on the paths.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, we can say that parents have to control their children but we know that, in reality, this might not be possible at all times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do appreciate that we have set speed limits but how will a user of a conventional bicycle know what speed he or she is travelling at?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also appreciate that we have a new team to enforce these new regulations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But with a vast amount of public paths, we all know that enforcement will be limited as we simply cannot be everywhere at all times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, will it be possible to make it mandatory for all riders to install and switch on their headlights at night on their bicycles, PMDs and PABs, especially since the probability of an accident increases when it is dark?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can we also consider making it compulsory for riders of bicycles, PMDs and PABs to dismount and push their bicycles, PMDs and PABs at crowded areas, for example, near bus stops?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even if the riders keep to the speed limits at these areas, it is unlikely to prevent accidents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would be much safer for all users if they dismount and push.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also clarify if the rules will or can apply to walkways in front of shops and along HDB void decks, lift lobbies and staircases?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A resident wrote to me recently; allow me to read out her concerns. "I would like to highlight that there has been an increasing number of people using bicycles, e-scooters and hoverboards at the walkway along the shops opposite my place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is there any way to put up signs to advise these riders to dismount from their mobile vehicles when they are at the walkway?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the walkway getting very crowded, there are riders who disregard the safety of pedestrians walking along the shops.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would seem like we are creating a loophole in this piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, I note that the Government had accepted in full the recommendations submitted by the Active Mobility Advisory Panel in March 2016.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I welcome the Government's move to include stakeholders in policy-making − in this case, 14 representatives from seniors and grassroots leaders to PMD users and cyclists.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is reminiscent of the Animal Welfare Legislation Review Committee, which I was a part of.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I look forward to more of such review and advisory committees being set up to ensure that the policies we enact are by the people and for the people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They help reduce our carbon footprint and shift Singapore towards a car-lite society.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They also empower many Singaporeans to go about their chores and carry out their jobs and they also connect us better with nature.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: While we want to encourage the use of such devices, more structure has to be in place for their usage.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As such, I would like to make three suggestions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: First, it will be great if we can put in place more infrastructure for our mobility devices.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: If there is budget room for it, could the Ministry of Finance provide LTA with more funding, especially for HDB towns which have a higher traffic density?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I am not asking this for all towns but just towns which have higher density.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Second, in private estates with many seniors, public paths need to be adapted to the usage of PMDs and PABs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This helps our seniors to access key amenities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I hope LTA can allocate a small dedicated budget for such purposes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In my constituency of Kebun Baru, there is a landed precinct called the Teachers' Housing Estate.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Many retired teachers and residents are giving up their cars as they grow older.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, they have difficulty accessing key amenities, especially given the hilly terrain that they live in.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They will be deeply appreciative if LTA can adapt footpaths to overcome the hilly terrains and perhaps create one or two small rain shelters on their way to key amenities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Again, I am not asking for a large sum but just small sums to examine the link between specific estates with ageing populations and key locations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The devices are fairly new to Singapore and it is necessary for the public to understand how to use them to their own benefit and not to endanger themselves or pedestrians.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: To achieve that, we can do a few things.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: One, include the Active Mobility framework to drivers' education because I think the drivers should know how mobility devices and users work as well.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Two, work with the Road Safety Council and cover this topic during excursions to our Road Safety Park for younger riders.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Three, advertise in cinemas which will reach out to more younger people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And fourth, engage in merging social media platforms, such as Mothership or even SGAG.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Third of all, I think we should also ensure affordable devices are available while we push for stronger safety standards.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It would also be good if LTA can publish the entire approved list of devices online.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: While LTA moves from throttle to throttle-less, what happens is that the ones available on the market are largely China-made ones.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For a brief moment of time, they were being excluded from being purchased.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The consumers were suddenly left with buying much more expensive PABs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I know LTA is working hard to identify and approve the lower cost ones from other parts of the world, but I hope that LTA can do more and move quickly to approve those.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can LTA elaborate on the circumstances that will usually entail a jail sentence?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: To allow us to tap on the Bill's full potential, we will need to create more infrastructure, raise awareness, and ensure safe but affordable options.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There has been more than a dozen Members who have spoken and it will take me a bit of time to respond to as many of the questions that had been raised as possible.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I hope that Members will bear with me.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A common concern voiced by Members is the need to protect users of public paths against dangerous conduct by a minority of reckless users.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, Members acknowledge the many benefits when bicycles and PMDs are used responsibly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We should, therefore, aim to strike a balance with rules which offer good protection and yet enable the vast majority of responsible cyclists and PMD users to continue riding on public paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This Bill gives legal effect to an initial set of rules that aims to do just that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I stress that it is an initial set of rules.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As they are implemented and with the benefit of experience, they can be refined in the future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In that spirit, I would like to share our present views on Members' suggestions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and other Members asked if we can do more to ensure that victims involved in accidents are assured of compensation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Sitoh, together with Mr Zainal Sapari, Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Joan Pereira suggested mandating third-party insurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Zainal Sapari shared with us the heart-wrenching circumstances of his resident.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In accidents involving serious injuries and damages, like Mdm Ang's case, the Police will investigate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If a cyclist or PMD user is found to be at fault, he may be prosecuted and the Court will consider if compensation should be paid, in addition to all the other penalties that the perpetrator will be liable for.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: By laying down the rules and code of conduct for cyclists and PMD users, this Bill will facilitate the Court process.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, we encourage frequent cyclists and PMD users to buy third-party insurance which is already available in the market.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For now, such insurance will not be mandatory.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This recognises the fact that there is a broad range of cyclists and PMD users − from those who cycle long distances daily, to those who use it occasionally for short errands; from very young children and working people, to seniors; and from the more affluent, to the less well-off who see cycling as an affordable means of getting around.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Insurance comes at some cost − not an insignificant amount − and it is not clear right now who should be targeted for mandatory insurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Cities with a strong culture of active mobility, such as Amsterdam and Copenhagen, likewise do not mandate insurance, but instead focus on cultivating safe and responsible behaviours.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked what pedestrians can do in hit-and-run accidents, if there are no witnesses present.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Pedestrians should note down the description of the device and the user and make a Police report as soon as possible, so that the Police can investigate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To deter hit-and-run accidents, we have also made it an offence if a cyclist, PMD user or PAB user fails to stop and render assistance and report the accident to the Police.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is a serious offence; that is why there is a possibility of a jail term.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked whether we will stipulate guidelines on the minimum width of public paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will take time, but we will certainly look into expanding the network of cycling paths and widened footpaths, and also the options available in private or mature estates, which Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Kok Heng Leun recommended, together with "ride-calming" measures which Mr Ang Hin Kee suggested.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Bill will also give LTA the necessary powers to remove obstructions from our public paths to make sure that pedestrians, cyclists and users of PABs and PMDs are able to use the widened paths fully, an issue which Miss Cheryl Chan raised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun had asked what is meant by "obstructions".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Basically, things that are left there that would cause users of the paths to have to try and, in Hokkien, we say "siam" or "get out of the way".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you make people "siam", you are causing an obstruction; I think we can understand that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin asked how the Bill will affect Town Councils, since public paths include common property managed by Town Councils.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Town Councils will continue to maintain these paths; there is no change to this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As the lead agency for active mobility, LTA will enforce against offences on public paths, including those within Town Councils' common property, to ensure that the application of the rules is consistent and minimise confusion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We accept that this will be our responsibility.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin will appreciate that this is not an easy task; LTA will engage Town Councils to see how their by-laws can be aligned with this Bill, and also how Town Councils and LTA can work together to strengthen enforcement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the same way, LTA cannot compel private land owners to allow paths of their land to become public paths, unless they agree to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This was a clarification sought by Mr Kok Heng Leun.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If, however, the private land owners enter into an access agreement with LTA and allow part of their private land to be converted into public paths, they, like Town Councils, still retain the responsibility for maintenance and liability.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is dependent on whether they agree with this arrangement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng, Mr Ang Hin Kee and Dr Teo Ho Pin commented on the classification of public paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have categorised the various types of paths based on their design.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The use of bicycles, PMDs and PABs will, therefore, be allowed, and these will be marked clearly at regular intervals and at cross junctions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Mr Melvin Yong noted, this will enhance safety for the riders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These will be clearly marked by signs at the entrances and exits of the bridges.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To address Assoc Prof Randolph Tan's query, these rules must be followed strictly and exceptions are only allowed when it is unsafe or impossible to do so, for example, if there are obstructions on the paths which riders are supposed to use but you have to "siam".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To avoid confusing the public, we do not expect to make significant changes to the way paths are classified, but we will closely monitor accident statistics and public feedback and adjust the classification of certain locations if necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Skates are relatively small, unlike skate scooters which are larger.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, pedestrians wearing skates can use pedestrian-only paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members have also suggested how some of the regulations can be further tightened.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked if there could be a minimum age limit for users of PMDs or have varying age limits for different types of PMDs, while Mr Zainal Sapari suggested an age criterion for riding PABs on roads.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During patrols conducted in the last few months, LTA has stopped several hundred errant cyclists and PMD users.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The offenders come from all age groups and it is now clear that safety-consciousness is not a matter of age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is, therefore, important to focus on education and enforcement, to ensure that all PMD users, regardless of age, are aware of the rules and use PMDs in a safe manner.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this regard, I agree that we should start teaching safe cycling and good riding habits from a young age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We must start when they are young and just learning for the first time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Which is why students are one of our key target groups for LTA's Safe Cycling Programme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Melvin Yong suggested that the Bill require active mobility users to wear protective gear.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The law already requires PAB users to wear helmets when riding on roads, because of the speed at which these motorised devices can travel and the higher level of danger when interacting with cars and heavy transport.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: PMDs are not allowed on roads, and so the same consideration does not apply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When cycling or riding on paths where it is relatively safer, the use of helmets is not mandatory but certainly recommended in the code of conduct.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What I am distributing is an infographic that shows the regulations as well as the Code of Conduct when riding on paths as well as on roads.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if I could refer Members to the second page where the title says "When riding on paths (proposed regulations)".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you look at the top right picture, it says "switch on front white lights and rear red lights in the dark".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee suggested that we ban the use of bicycles and PABs on certain roads with high speed limits and heavy vehicular traffic.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We already prohibit cycling on expressways and on certain roads where there are safety concerns, such as the Fort Canning Road tunnel.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Naturally, this rule should be extended to PABs as well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To address Assoc Prof Randolph Tan's concern, the existing regulations also require cyclists and PAB users riding on the roads to signal their intentions in time to give other road users enough time to react.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will monitor the situation and, if justified, consider extending registration to all motorised devices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Miss Cheryl Chan as well as Mr Pritam Singh sought clarifications regarding the regulations for sellers of non-compliant devices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should first point out that clause 34 clearly bans the sale of non-compliant devices for use on public paths, and this provision applies to all commercial sales, which Mr Ang Hin Kee supports.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Mr Ang Hin Kee correctly points out, sellers have a duty to educate buyers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Clauses 33 and 34, therefore, require sellers to prove they have advised buyers accordingly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is part of their duty to educate the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The objective of clause 30, which makes it an offence to openly display non-compliant PMDs, is to target those who attempt to retail such devices directly to consumers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It does not apply to one-off sales, such as the sale of a second-hand device from one individual to another, or wholesale trade, as devices sold through these channels may not be intended for use on our public paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Clause 20, which Mr Dennis Tan sought clarification on, gives the Government flexibility to, except certain devices from the roads if they merit exception as new models emerge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have no plans to do so but the flexibility is there.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There was a question: why do we not simply ban the importation of non-compliant devices?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I can understand that our instinct is to say just ban it; make it easier, straightforward.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But firstly, there is no reason to ban the use of such non-compliant devices on private property on private land.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not likely that many people will do so but if, indeed, there are people who want to do that, there is no reason to ban it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It may be excessive, it may be hard to even pass muster with the trade agreements that we are a part of.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Melvin Yong asked whether our regulations apply to online sellers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Non-compliant devices are also liable to seizure and forfeiture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The harsh penalties serve as a deterrent against buying these devices, whether from online or brick-and-mortar shops.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For consistency and protection of all path users, we cannot offer a one-off amnesty to existing non-compliant devices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope Mr Dennis Tan can support such a stand.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Clauses 26 and 27, the intention is really not to impose cost but to share responsibility and ensure that private developers as well as building owners take ownership of the signages and the way-finding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, they are quite similar to existing requirements that the Building and Construction Authority and the Urban Redevelopment Authority impose.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is nothing very new about it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Many Members, including Mr Dennis Tan, have called for strong enforcement, and asked how LTA plans to step it up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: LTA's enforcement officers target hotspot areas, such as near crowded bus stops and traffic junctions, where there is high interaction pedestrians, cyclists and PMD users.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: LTA officers are also deployed in response to public feedback about problem areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To complement their efforts, LTA will examine how best to deploy technologies, such as speed guns and CCTV cameras.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our officers will also be supported by more than 600 volunteers from the grassroots, whose enforcement powers include documenting photo and video evidence and obtaining personal particulars from suspected offenders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These volunteers will be trained on the scope of their enforcement powers, how to record evidence, as well as key communication skills, which Assoc Prof Randolph Tan spoke about, such as how to engage errant cyclists and PMD users and educate the public about safe behaviour while riding on public paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Zainal Sapari suggested imposing harsh penalties for active mobility users riding under the influence of alcohol.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is twice the penalty for first-time offenders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: While Mr Henry Kwek commented that imprisonment may be a harsh punishment, in some cases, this may be justified, as the offences could lead to injury or even death.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Courts will decide on the sentencing based on the facts of the case.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition to on-road accidents, we will also keep track of off-road accidents, to better study trends and make adjustments to the rules and penalties as necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng asked how cyclists, PMD users and PAB users would know their speeds.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can purchase a speedometer for their devices or download free or low-cost mobile apps that function as speedometers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I should add that, if in the first place they did not buy a non-compliant device, the risk of violating the speed limits is low.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Notwithstanding the speed limits, cyclists, PMD users and PAB users should always put safety first; they should make it a habit to be cautious, especially in crowded areas, and dismount whenever and wherever necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will do well to remember what Mr Kok Heng Leun reminded us earlier − his comments about civility.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Offenders of compoundable offences, such as reckless riding, may also be required to attend the Safe Cycling Programme as one of the conditions of composition.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Dennis Tan suggested that the Government step up and sustain our education efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We agree and we have introduced many initiatives to educate the public about safety.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, LTA launched the Safe Riders Campaign in April 2016 to raise awareness about safe and gracious sharing of paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has conducted engagement sessions with community leaders, retailers and interest groups, so that they can help spread the safe riding message.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Following the passing of the Bill, the rules will be publicised widely through easy-to-understand infographics, which I distributed earlier, and disseminated through newspaper advertisements, social media, as well as pamphlets and posters.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: LTA is also working closely with major PMD retailers to educate consumers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Henry Kwek helpfully suggested a number of mass media and social media platforms to publicise our messages.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have also enlisted the help of volunteers under our Active Mobility Patrol scheme, who have been patrolling neighbourhoods to spread the message of safety.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We already have the support of 37 constituencies and one non-government organisation which, together, have rallied some 600 volunteers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope to count on your support to expand these efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Before closing, I will briefly respond in Mandarin to comments made by Mr Ang Hin Kee.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Ang Hin Kee has raised several valuable suggestions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We should, indeed, regulate importers and retailers of PABs and PMDs strictly; and we should punish those retailers that sell non-compliant devices and workshops that illegally modify devices to ensure that motorised devices used in Singapore meet our safety standards.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We treat all sellers equally; however, it is more challenging to enforce against overseas online retailers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, we will mete out stiff penalties to those who buy non-compliant devices and use them on public paths in Singapore, as deterrence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We should also step up on our plans to build more public infrastructure so that it will be more convenient for users to park, use and store their devices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the next few years, LTA will build more bicycle parking lots island-wide.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At present, we do not have storage facilities specifically designed for PMDs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, PMDs tend to be small and light, and most users carry them around.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the number of PMD users increasing and more varieties of PMDs becoming available, we will consider adding appropriate storage facilities for them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides this, Mr Ang Hin Kee also stressed the importance of increasing safety awareness among the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I fully agree with this and I urge all Members to help spread the message of our new rules and regulations and encourage more residents to join our team of active mobility volunteers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the next few years, MOT and LTA will closely monitor the increasing usage of active mobility devices and continuously refine our rules and regulations based on public feedback.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In English): This Bill seeks to ensure that safety on our public paths is not compromised, even as we encourage active mobility.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will keep an open mind and continue to review our rules.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I noted earlier, this is unlikely to be the final set of regulations for active mobility.
